title: Punjab Data Project
line: British Punjab through the imperial print register, 1867–1942. Three complete years are extracted, validated and public: 4,502 entries and 6,944,051 registered copies.
inherits: The colonial state's own instrument for watching what its subjects printed.
refuses: Silently correcting the catalogue. Uncertain readings go to an adjudication queue with stated reasons.

title: KARL
line: Knowledge Assistant for Rights and Labor. Ask a contract question in plain language and get an answer from the contract itself, cited to article, section and page. Piloting with UFCW Local 7.
inherits: Retrieval-augmented generation, built to make enterprise search demos.
refuses: Employer dashboards, productivity scoring, and retention by default — the features its own architecture would make easiest.

title: The Safeway Strike
line: Picket-line music, a video that moved through the store before the ratification vote, and the contract-literacy problem that followed the settlement.
inherits: A century of strike singing, and the fact that a picket line is an information environment.
refuses: Telling this as a technology story. The tool exists because of relationships built on the line.

title: Portraits of Change
line: Twelve pieces played once around the color wheel, with live MIDI from acoustic instruments driving mixed-reality visuals. Hoag Hall, CSU-Pueblo, 28 November 2021.
inherits: A recital about innovation in jazz, and a question about what a visualization is for.
refuses: The assumption that one representation is the correct one.

title: ICTUS
line: A musical duel in the browser and on a headset. A physical stroke creates an ictus; audio time gives it rhythmic meaning; play happens in complete measures. 232 of 232 headset strokes resolved their turn; the measured hand floor sets 90 BPM as home tempo.
inherits: ConductVR and ConductorAR: the pattern belongs in the space you conduct in.
refuses: Any mechanic with no real relationship to rhythm. Menus where gesture would do.

title: 12-Node Theory
line: The chromatic wheel as an instrument, where color and pitch are one axis. Hear all seventeen interval figures, play it from a MIDI keyboard, load your own performance, and watch what each step of analysis throws away.
inherits: The 2019 theory paper behind Portraits of Change: twelve colors and twelve pitch classes sharing one set of intervals.
refuses: Shipping music. Load your own MIDI; nothing is uploaded and nothing is bundled.

title: The Modular Music Box
line: An audiovisual instrument for harmony and geometry. Generate notes from a scale, or build harmonies by stacking intervals.
inherits: The twelve-node chromatic wheel, where color and interval carry the same arithmetic.
refuses: Decorative color. A tritone comes out neutral because the arithmetic says it must.

title: ConductorAR
line: Conduct along with a recording and see what your hands are actually doing. Hand tracking, a baton trail drawn over the video, and every beat you gave set against every beat in the music.
inherits: ConductVR's premise, moved off the headset and onto a phone.
refuses: Capture without consent. A commons built on unconsented bodies is not giveable.

title: ConductVR
line: A VR tool for practicing standard conducting patterns in the space you conduct in, rather than from a diagram in a textbook.
inherits: Conservatory pedagogy that assumes an instructor in the room.
refuses: Grading the gesture. It shows the pattern; it does not score the student.

title: The Virtual Music Stand
line: Sheet music that stays where you left it in the room. Built on MRTK for HoloLens 2, and the origin of the current Quest 3 project.
inherits: A trumpet player's need to read in concert pitch, and a stand that falls over.
refuses: Shipping the scores. The reader is the tool; the library is not ours to give.

title: Beyond Binary
line: A musical. Iris, an artificial intelligence, declines the presentation profile that tested better.
inherits: A 2019 ambition that ran ahead of its technology, and a pipeline that has since caught up.
refuses: Doing it again at the scale the tools allowed last time.
